page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top, with page number 575 at the upper right. Then italic question headings and paragraphs, a rule, a large division heading (titulus) with a Latin and black-letter German title, and further italic headings and paragraphs. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword or signature.

main_text.l: Quid Animalium nomine proditum est?
ANimalium nomine, quae ratione carent, si qua
lascivia, aut pavore, aut feritate pauperiem fece-
rint: Noxalis actio lege duodecim tabularum pro-
dita est. Quae animalia si noxae dedantur, proficiunt
reo ad liberationem. in princ. inst. eod.
Quid est pauperies?
Pauperies est damnum sine injuria facientis da-
tum. Nec enim potest animal injuriam fecisse dici,
quod sensu caret. in princ. verf. pauperies. inst. eod.
Quidnam ædilitio edicto prohibetur?
Sciendum est ædilitio edicto prohiberi nos canes,
verrem, aprum, ursum,
leonem ibi habere, quà
vulgo iter fit.[?] §. cæterum. inst. eod.
QU-
IS EST DECIMUS
Titulus?
De iis, per quos agere possumus. Von

l.bl: denen durch welche wir klagen vnd rechtlich

main_text.l: Cujus nomine agere possumus?
ADmonendi sumus agere posse quemlibet homi-
nem, aut suo nomine, aut alieno. Alieno, veluti
procuratorio, tutorio, in princ. inst. eo.
Quomodo constituitur procurator?
Procurator (ein[?] [illegible, ~8 letters]) neque certis verbis, neque
praesente semper adversario, imo plerunque eo igno-
rante constituitur: cuicunque enim permissum est rem
tuam agere, aut defendere: is tuus procurator intel-
ligitur. §. procurator. inst. eod.

page.notes: The Greek word in parentheses after "Procurator" is not legible at this scan resolution; it is marked illegible. The "ein" before it is doubtful. The Latin "ADmonendi" has a large initial A joined to the word. "homi-nem" breaks across lines with no printed hyphen visible; written whole. "fit" after "iter" is doubtful (the scan looks like "lit" or "fit"). The German subtitle is set in black letter and is marked with bl. The large initial V in "Von" is decorative and is written as V. The heading "QUIS EST DECIMUS Titulus?" is the division heading; "Titulus" is set in italic type in the original.
